advocate: Ad + vocare: call to defend. An advocate speaks for the cause.
Advocate sounds like avocat: both speak for you.
appreciable: Appreciate: measure the value. An appreciable gain: big enough to notice.
Appreciable: you can see the difference.
apprehension: Apprehendre: to seize. Apprehension: fear grips you before the exam.
Apprehension also = arrest: seized by police.
archaic: Arche: beginning. An archaic word is from the beginning of time.
Archaic: dusty, from the Stone Age.
ascendancy: Ascendere: climb. Rise to ascendancy: top position.
autonomously: Auto + nomos: self-law. A robot working autonomously.
boon: Bon: good. A boon for the economy.
consummate: Consummare: complete. A consummate liar: perfect at it.
Consummate: the master at his craft.
dearth: Dear = costly; dearth: scarcity raises prices. A dearth of talent.
degrade: De + gradus: step down. Plastic degrades slowly.
deter: De + terrere: scare off. High fines deter speeding.
discriminate: Discernere: tell apart. A discriminating palate.
disenfranchise: Dis + franchise: strip the vote. Laws disenfranchised citizens.
disheartened: Dis + heart: lose heart. Disheartened by failure.
elusive: E + ludere: slip away in play. An elusive fugitive.
Elusive: hard to pin down, like a fish.
endemic: En + demos: in the people. Malaria is endemic to the region.
entice: En + titio: firebrand. Entice with sweets.
fete: Fête: a party. To fête the winners.
Fete: lavish celebration in someone’s honour.
fledgling: Fledge: grow feathers. A fledgling company.
flounder: Flounder fish thrashing on the sand. Flounder in an interview.
guffaw: Imitates the sound. A guffaw from the back row.
impede: In + pes: foot-shackle. Roadworks impede traffic.
impermeable: Im + permeare: can’t pass through. Impermeable raincoat.
Impermeable to criticism: it bounces off.
incessant: In + cessare: no stop. Incessant rain.
inclement: In + clemens: not mild. Inclement weather.
ingenuity: Ingenium: talent. Ingenuity solves problems with little.
malady: Mal habitus: poor condition. A mysterious malady.
Malady: an illness, a social ill.
meander: Maeander river: winding. A stream meanders.
Meander: a walk without a destination.
moot: Moot: a meeting to debate. A moot point is arguable (UK) or pointless (US).
Moot: the question no longer matters.
morose: Mos: mood. A morose patient says nothing.
muted: Mute: silent. Muted colours, muted applause.
patronize: Pater: father. Don’t patronize me: talk down.
pithy: Pith: the core. A pithy slogan.
plodding: Plod: heavy steps. A plodding pace.
proponent: Pro + ponere: put forward. A proponent of free trade.
Proponent: the champion of an idea.
quandary: Quandary: perplexity. In a quandary about two jobs.
raffish: Riff-raff with charm. A raffish grin.
renege: Re + negare: deny. Renege on a deal.
respite: Respectus: look back; a break. A brief respite.
Respite: a pause from the storm.
robust: Robust: strong enough to withstand tests.
snide: Snide: a dig with a smirk.
stolid: Stolidus: dull. A stolid face shows no feeling.
thwart: Thwart: across. Rain thwarted the picnic.
